This means if a queen is at $(r, c)$, no other queen can be at $(r-1, c-1), (r-1, c), (r-1, c+1), (r, c-1), (r, c+1), (r+1, c-1), (r+1, c), (r+1, c+1)$. Wait, the rule says "Queens may not touch, including diagonally." This is the standard "no touching" constraint often found in puzzles like this. It implies that for any two queens at $(r_1, c_1)$ and $(r_2, c_2)$, $|r_1 - r_2| \le 1$ implies $|c_1 - c_2| > 1$. Actually, let's re-read carefully: "Queens may not touch, including diagonally. Thus queens in consecutive rows cannot occupy columns differing by 1." This confirms the standard non-attacking constraint for adjacent rows, but specifically forbids touching. It also says "Queens separated by more than one row MAY share a long diagonal". This is a crucial distinction from standard N-Queens. Standard N-Queens forbids *any* diagonal sharing. This puzzle only forbids *touching*. So, $(1,1)$ and $(3,3)$ are allowed because they don't touch. $(1,1)$ and $(2,2)$ are not allowed.
